questions.question: What makes a plan a feasible solution of an optimization model?
options: It values every variable and meets all constraints, signs included
It values every variable and meets all constraints except sign rules
It values every variable and has the best value of the objective
It values every variable and meets most of the model's constraints

questions.question: A model has variables $x_1,x_2,x_3$ and three constraints. A proposal fixes $x_1=2$ and $x_2=5$, which satisfy every constraint that involves only $x_1$ and $x_2$, and leaves $x_3$ open. Is it a feasible solution?
options: Not yet, since every variable must be given a value first
Yes, as all the constraints it can be checked against hold
Yes, as $x_3$ is taken to be 0 unless stated otherwise
No, as a plan with an open variable breaks every constraint

questions.question: A plan satisfies nine of a model's ten constraints and breaks the tenth. How is it classified?
options: As feasible, since nearly all of the constraints hold
As feasible if the tenth is only a minor constraint
As infeasible only if the tenth one is an equality
As infeasible, as one violated constraint suffices

questions.question: Is every feasible solution of a profit-maximization model also a best allowed plan?
options: No; feasibility is needed for being best but is not enough
Yes; any plan meeting all constraints is equally good
No; a best plan may break constraints in order to earn more
Yes, provided that its objective value is positive

questions.question: A model has the constraint $2x_1+x_2\le9$. A plan gives $2x_1+x_2=9$ and satisfies all other constraints. Is it feasible?
options: Yes; equality satisfies a $\le$ constraint
No; $\le$ needs the left side below 9
No; plans on a constraint's bound are excluded
Only if the constraint is written with $=$

questions.question: A production plan $(x_1,x_2)=(4,-1)$ is checked against the constraints $x_1+x_2\le6$, $x_1-x_2\le5$, $x_1\ge0$ and $x_2\ge0$. Is it feasible?
options: Yes; both functional constraints hold for $(4,-1)$
No; $x_1-x_2=5$ breaks the constraint $x_1-x_2\le5$
Yes; sign conditions are not real constraints
No; $x_2=-1$ breaks the sign condition $x_2\ge0$

questions.question: In a model the two variables must add up to exactly 10, $x_1+x_2=10$, with $x_1\le7$ and both variables nonnegative. Which plan is allowed?
A model has the constraints $x_1+x_2\le6$, $x_1-x_2\le3$, $x_1\ge0$ and $x_2\ge0$. Which of the plans $(0,0)$, $(3,3)$, $(5,1)$ and $(2,3)$ are feasible?
options: All four of the plans

questions.question: A model's objective is changed from total profit to total cost, while its variables and constraints stay the same. How does this change which plans are feasible?
options: Fewer plans are feasible, as high-cost plans drop out
Not at all; feasibility does not involve the objective
More plans are feasible, as low-profit plans now count
It depends on the coefficients of the new objective

questions.question: Integer restrictions are added to a model whose variables could previously take fractional values. What happens to its feasible solutions?
options: Fractional ones may be lost; no new feasible solutions appear
New feasible solutions appear, namely the whole-number plans
Nothing changes, as fractional plans can always be rounded
Whole-number plans become infeasible and fractional ones remain

questions.question: For each constraint of a model there is some plan that satisfies it. Does it follow that the model has a feasible solution?
options: Yes; the plans for the separate constraints can always be combined into one
Yes, as long as every one of the constraints is a linear inequality
No, but only when at least one of the constraints is an equality
No; the constraints must hold together, and two of them may contradict

questions.question: Fix $x_1=4$ in a model with the constraints $x_1+2x_2\le16$, $3x_1+x_2\le20$ and $x_2\ge1$. Which range of $x_2$ keeps the plan $(4,x_2)$ feasible?
Variables $x_1,x_2$ count whole vehicles, and the constraints are $x_1+x_2\ge5$ and $2x_1+3x_2\le12$. Which plan is feasible?

A model makes $z=5x_1+4x_2$ as large as possible subject to $6x_1+4x_2\le24$, $x_1+2x_2\le6$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Among the plans $(4,0)$, $(3,1.5)$, $(2.4,1.8)$ and $(4,1)$, which has the highest value among those that are feasible?
In the constraint $2x_1+x_2\le b$, the right-hand side $b$ is raised from 100 to 120; the rest of the model is unchanged. Which statement about feasible solutions is always true?
options: Some plans feasible before become infeasible
Every plan infeasible before becomes feasible
Every plan feasible before is still feasible
The feasible solutions stay exactly the same

questions.question: A plan satisfies every constraint of a staffing model, but in practice it breaks a legal rest-time rule that the model does not contain. Is it a feasible solution of the model?
options: No; a plan that breaks a law can never be called feasible
Yes; feasibility concerns the stated constraints only
No; feasibility also covers rules the model left out
Yes, but only if its objective value is the best one

questions.question: The number $b$ is a given right-hand side in the two constraints $x_1+2x_2\le b$ and $2x_1-x_2\ge b-6$. Find all $b$ for which the plan $(3,2)$ satisfies both.
options: $b\ge7$
$7\le b\le10$

questions.question: Variables $x_1,x_2$ must be whole numbers with $x_1,x_2\ge0$, and the model has the constraint $2x_1+2x_2=5$. How many feasible solutions does it have?
options: Infinitely many
None at all
Exactly one
Exactly three
